newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Bullish Australian stocks soar to record close.
newsitem.headline: Bullish Australian stocks soar to record close.

text.p: SPI Futures 2620 +17 US 30yr cl 6.98 -0.05
10yrbond futs 92.540 +0.105 Gold NY 345.75 Lon fix 343.90
*Stocks shatter record highs and turnover marks as bourse bolts above 2,600 for first time ever. Volume 526.57 million, A$1.88 bln value, 1,157 stocks traded, 316 steady, 535 up, 306 down.
A bullish Australian share market bolted above the 2,600 level for the first time ever on Friday, shattering turnover milestones and previous records on the way.
The All Ordinaries index soared 19.9 points to a record closing level of 2,610.5, having touched a record high of 2,617.4, easily surpassing Thursday's record high of 2,591.5.
June share price index futures were 17 points higher at 2,620, a 9.5 point premium to the underlying index.
The hat trick of records was completed by an impressive, albeit options-boosted, A$1.88 billion turnover. The previous record turnover was A$1.74 billion on December 20, 1996.
"It's been a fantastic market, particularly BHP," said Reynolds and Co dealer, Grant Williams, although he noted gains were widespread with healthy buying interest across the board.
"But other things like ANZ have carried it along as well. There seems to be quite a demand for good stocks at the moment."

BHP posted a gain of 1.4 percent to close at A$18.86, still recovering after its sharp selldown after its fourth quarter profit warning on Monday, and aided by the resetting of positions after Thursday's May series option expiries.
"Given the options expiry yesterday, there may well have been some short covering today," Williams said.
Others concurred, although they said other factors had also boosted the bellwether.

"They are running ahead on some of their new projects and I think the market has factored that in, plus it always helps if you have a little oil discovery as well," said Daiwa Securities dealer, Mark Pervan, noting Thursday's Algerian oil find.
ANZ Bank was the strongest performer among the banks, adding nearly three percent to A$8.99, while National Australia Bank ended 1.2 percent up at A$18.78.
It was not all rosy for all of the big four though, with Westpac and Commonwealth Bank largely ignored.

Westpac ended just a cent higher at A$7.13 after spending most of the day below square, while Commonwealth Bank fell victim to an afternoon ambush by sellers who slashed 1.8 percent off the stock by the close. Commonwealth Bank closed at A$14.12.
Brokers cited switching to the more attractive ANZ Bank and National Australia Bank, as well as quality of earnings issues.
"ANZ 's result compared to Westpac just shows up the difference between the two," said Reynolds' Williams.
Chemicals group ICI Australia closed up four cents at A$12.15 after anouncing a buyback of A$360 million worth of its parent ICI Plc's stake.

Action continued in the second tier oils, with Cultus Petroleum again strongly sought after Thursday's reserve estimate upgrade at the Cornea oil field offshore Western Australia. Cultus shares added 3.5 percent to A$3.90, while Novus Petroleum added 1.7 percent to A$4.83, hitting a record high A$4.85 on the way.
Boral starred among the building materials group, jumping 10 to A$4.19. The sector index jumped 1.3 percent.
Rises convincingly outnumbered falls by a ratio of about nine to five, while only about 27 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
FUTURES/OPTIONS - Heavy derivatives activity followed the lead of the underlying markets with 71,538 (62,807) options traded and June SPI contracts turnover totalling 7,972 (5,420).

In other local markets, Australian debt yields fell sharply across the curve after a weak April retail trade data added fuel to talk that the Reserve Bank's easing cycle is not over yet. By 5.30 p.m. (0730 GMT), 10 year T-bonds were yielding 7.47 percent, compared to Thursday's 7.57 percent.
The Australian dollar was robbed of a hard won rally to end at three month lows Friday after shockingly weak retail trade data left the market looking down the barrel of a rate cut.
By 5.30 p.m. (0730 GMT), the dollar had fled to US$0.7604/09, its lowest local close since February 12, from an early US$0.7659/64 and US$0.7652/57 late here Thursday.
